content:
Marta: Heads up — since ~09:20 PST we’re seeing a spike in DNS timeouts for service-to-service calls inside gpu-pool nodes (us-west2). model-router -> model-backend calls failing, p95 latency up to 800ms, lots of 503/504s :frowning:

Devon: saw the same in our e2e runs, readiness probes flapping on model-backend. Any recent infra changes?

infra-bot: alert: 5xx_rate(model-backend) > 5% over 10m

Phil: we rolled kernel 5.15.0-83 on gpu nodes last night. Could be MTU/RDMA interplay.

Marta: I ran a quick dig from a failing node:
```
$ dig @127.0.0.53 model-backend.svc.cluster.local +short
; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```

Devon: coreDNS logs show lots of "read udp ...: i/o timeout" and fallback to TCP in traces. snippet:
```
2026-03-18T16:22:10Z [INFO] read udp 10.0.5.12:53832->10.0.0.10:53: i/o timeout
```

Marta: ping with 1400 payload between nodes shows fragmentation/loss:
```
ping -s 1400 10.0.5.14
--- 10.0.5.14 ping statistics ---
10 packets transmitted, 8 received, 20% packet loss
```

Aleena: could be MTU mismatch after rdma/eni path change. Check tc qdisc and iframesize. Also node-local DNS cache (nodelocaldns daemonset) logs show eviction thrash.

Devon: grabbing tcpdump on eth0 + rdma0 now, will check for ICMP frag or DF set.

Phil: quick mitigation ideas: prefer TCP for CoreDNS queries or increase CoreDNS replicas temporarily. Another option: clamp MTU on host to 8900 until we know root cause.

Marta: I'll try forcing node-local-dns to prefer TCP for lookups and enable more verbose logging. Also seeing conntrack spikes on kube-proxy in the GPU pool.

Devon: I see RDMA NIC driver upgrades in last kpatch. Rolling back one node to previous kernel and re-running probes.

Marta: action items:
- Devon: tcpdump + perf counters on gpu-123 (assigned)
- Phil: roll one node back to kernel r80 and test (assigned)
- Aleena: bump coredns max_concurrent and patch node-local-dns to log UDP fallback

Phil: temp note: if we see <3% drop after rollback -> confirm kernel. If not, inspect MTU along the entire path (host, overlay, ENI) and RDMA offload settings.

Devon: tcpdump shows lots of 'fragmentation needed' ICMP and some RDMA retransmits. example:
```
07:12:34.123456 IP 10.0.5.12 > 10.0.5.14: UDP, length 1420
07:12:34.123789 IP 10.0.5.14 > 10.0.5.12: ICMP frag needed, mtu 1420
```

Aleena: OK - MTU clamp seems likely. I'll push a kube-hostsys change to set MTU to 8920 across gpu nodes and monitor.

Marta: created incident doc: https://redwood/incidents/INC-2026-189 (pinned). Will update when metrics stable. :thumbsup:

Devon: rolling back kernel on gpu-123 now — will update with readiness results.

infra-bot: deploy: kernel-rollback to gpu-123 succeeded

Devon: model-backend readiness passed after rollback, dns timeouts drop to 0.8% and p95 down to ~120ms. Looks promising.

Phil: leave one node in rollback while Aleena applies MTU clamp; if stable, roll forward with kpatch fix.

Marta: closing loop: if this persists after MTU clamp we escalate to provider for RDMA path checks.

Aleena: monitoring dashboard: coreDNS udp_i/o_timeouts down to near zero after MTU change; will keep watch for 2 hrs.

Marta: great work all. :heart:
